Why This Book Exists


Have you ever wondered if God is real? Not just real in a general sense. Real in a way you could touch. Real in a way you could see. Real in a way you could sit with. A lot of people believe in something. A force. A universe. A higher power. But that is vague. That is far away. That is not personal.


Here is the surprising thing. The Bible does not describe a vague force. It describes a God who shows up. In person. In history. At specific times. In specific places. To specific people. He walks. He talks. He eats. He wrestles. He stands in a fire. He sits in a tent. He speaks from a bush. He is not a concept. He is a someone.


This book is about those encounters. Thirty of them. Real moments in ancient history where the invisible God became visible. Where the eternal God stepped into time. Where the pre-incarnate Christ, the Son of God before He was born in Bethlehem, showed up in the story.


This is for the seeker. For the curious. For the person who wants more than a feeling. This is for the one who wants evidence. The Bible is full of it. And these encounters are some of the most powerful evidence there is. God has been showing up for a very long time. He is still showing up. Let's go find Him.



The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will see God differently. Not as a distant idea. As a present person. You will see that the Son of God was not a surprise. He was not a backup plan. He was always there. In the garden. In the tent. In the fire. On the road. He has been visiting His people since the beginning.

The Hook


The very first encounter with God is a walk. Not a vision. Not a dream. Not a voice from the clouds. A walk. In a garden. In the cool of the day. God was walking. Adam and Eve heard His footsteps. That is the first picture of God in the Bible. A God who walks.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden." - Genesis 3:8


God walked. In a garden. With people. This is the beginning. This is the picture. God is not distant. He is not far. He is near. He is walking. He is looking for them. He is calling to them. "Where are you?" Not because He did not know. Because He wanted them to come out. He wanted to be with them. The walk was the relationship. The walk was the encounter.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son." - John 1:14


The God who walked in the garden is the God who walked the roads of Israel. Jesus is the walking God. He came near. He walked with us. He ate with us. He touched us. The garden walk was a preview. Jesus is the full picture. The pre-incarnate Christ was walking in the garden. He was the one they heard. He was the one they hid from. He is the one who came to find them.


The Verdict


The garden walk is a shadow. The earthly walk of Jesus is the substance. The God who walked is the God who came. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel like God is far away? Like He is somewhere out there and you are down here? Look at the garden. He was walking. He was looking. He was calling. He is still walking. He is still looking. He is still calling. He wants to be with you. Come out of hiding. Walk with Him.


The Prayer


God, thank you for walking. Thank you for looking. Thank you for calling. I have been hiding. I have been afraid. I am coming out. Walk with me. Be with me. I want to be near you. Amen.

The Hook


Three strangers showed up at Abraham's tent. One of them was God. Abraham did not know it at first. But he offered them food. He washed their feet. He made them dinner. And God sat at his table. God ate. God talked. God stayed. This is one of the most intimate encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. When he saw them, he hurried from the entrance of his tent to meet them and bowed low to the ground." - Genesis 18:2


Three men. One of them was the LORD. Abraham ran to them. He offered water. He offered bread. He offered rest. He made them a meal. He stood by them while they ate. The LORD ate at his table. The LORD talked with him. The LORD stayed. This is intimate. This is personal. This is God in person. The pre-incarnate Christ sat at a table with a man.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me." - Revelation 3:20


Jesus wants to eat with you. He wants to sit at your table. He wants to talk with you. He wants to stay. The tent meal is a shadow. The table of Jesus is the substance. He is knocking. He is waiting. He wants to come in. He wants to eat with you. Open the door. Let Him in.


The Verdict


The tent meal is a shadow. The table of Jesus is the substance. God wants to eat with you. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you want to eat with God? Do you want to sit at a table with Him? Do you want Him to stay? He is knocking. He is waiting. He wants to come in. He wants to eat with you. Open the door. Set the table. Let Him in. He will stay.


The Prayer


Jesus, come to my table. Come and sit. Come and eat. I want you here. Not just in the church. Not just in my prayers. At my table. In my home. Stay with me. Eat with me. Be with me. Amen.

The Hook


A bush on fire. But the bush does not burn up. Moses sees it. He walks closer. And God speaks. From the bush. The fire is the presence. The bush is the body. God is in the bush. And Moses is standing on holy ground. This is one of the most famous encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"There the angel of the LORD appeared to him in flames of fire from within a bush. Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up." - Exodus 3:2


The angel of the Lord appeared. In flames. From within a bush. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He is in the fire. He is in the bush. He is speaking. "Moses, Moses." He is calling. He is sending. The bush was burning. The fire was real. The presence was real. The encounter was real. And Moses was changed.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The God in the bush is the God in the body. Jesus is the burning bush. He is the fire in the bush. He is the presence in the person. The bush did not burn up. Jesus was not destroyed. The fire did not consume the bush. The grave did not consume Jesus. The burning bush is a shadow. The body of Jesus is the substance. The encounter is the same.


The Verdict


The bush is a shadow. The body is the substance. The fire is the presence. The person is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you want to encounter God? Do you want to hear His voice? Do you want to see His fire? Look at the bush. Look at Jesus. He is the one who shows up. He is the one who speaks. He is the one who calls. He is calling you. Take off your shoes. You are on holy ground. Listen.


The Prayer


God, thank you for the fire. Thank you for the bush. Thank you for speaking. I am listening. I am here. I am on holy ground. Speak to me. Call me. Send me. I am yours. Amen.

The Hook


Hagar was a servant. She was running away. She was pregnant. She was alone. She was in the desert. And an angel found her. The angel of the Lord. He spoke to her. He promised her a future. And she gave God a name. "You are the God who sees me." This is one of the most tender encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The angel of the LORD found Hagar near a spring in the desert... She gave this name to the LORD who spoke to her: 'You are the God who sees me.'" - Genesis 16:7, 13


The angel of the Lord found Hagar. She was a nobody. She was a runaway. She was a servant. But the angel found her. He saw her. He spoke to her. He promised her. She named God "the God who sees." Because He saw her. In the desert. Alone. Unimportant. He saw her. The pre-incarnate Christ saw her. He came to her. He spoke to her. He sees you too.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us." - Romans 5:8


God saw us in our sin. God saw us in our lostness. God saw us in our desert. He did not wait for us to clean up. He came. He died. He found us. The angel who saw Hagar is the Christ who sees you. He is the God who sees. He is the God who comes. He is the God who saves.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. The God who sees is the God who comes. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel invisible? Do you feel like nobody sees you? Do you feel like you are in the desert and no one knows? You are seen. The God who sees you is here. He knows your name. He knows your pain. He sees you. He comes to you. You are not invisible to Him.


The Prayer


God, you see me. You see my desert. You see my pain. You see my loneliness. Thank you for seeing me. Thank you for coming to me. Thank you for knowing my name. I am not invisible to you. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook


Jacob was alone. He was scared. He was about to face his brother who wanted to kill him. And a man came. And they wrestled. All night. In the dark. In the dirt. And Jacob would not let go. The man was God. Jacob wrestled with God. And he walked away with a limp and a blessing. This is one of the strangest and most powerful encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"So Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him till daybreak... Then the man said, 'Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with humans and have overcome.'" - Genesis 32:24, 28


Jacob wrestled with God. In the dark. In the dirt. He held on. He would not let go. He said, "I will not let you go unless you bless me." And God blessed him. God changed his name. God changed his life. The pre-incarnate Christ wrestled with Jacob. He let Himself be grabbed. He let Himself be held. He let Himself be wounded. And He blessed him. This is the God who lets you grab Him.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"But we see Jesus, who was made lower than the angels for a little while, now crowned with glory and honor because he suffered death." - Hebrews 2:9


Jacob wrestled a man. The man was God. God let Himself be grabbed. God let Himself be held. He could have broken free. He did not. This is a picture of Jesus. Jesus let Himself be grabbed, beaten, and held on a cross. He did not break free. He let Himself be held. For us. The wrestler is a shadow. The cross is the substance.


The Verdict


The wrestler is a shadow. The cross is the substance. God lets Himself be grabbed. God lets Himself be held. God lets Himself be wounded. For us. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you struggling? Are you angry? Do you want to grab God and shout? Do it. He can handle it. He is not fragile. Jacob held on and did not let go. Hold on. Even in the dark. Even in the dirt. He is there. He will bless you.


The Prayer


God, I am struggling. I am not going to let go. I am holding on to you. Even if I limp away, I am not letting go until you bless me. You are worth holding. You are worth the fight. I am not letting go. Amen.

The Hook


Joshua was about to fight the biggest battle of his life. He was camped near Jericho. He looked up and saw a man. The man had a sword drawn. Joshua was bold. He asked the question. "Are you for us or for our enemies?" The answer changed everything. "Neither. I am the commander of the army of the Lord."


The Ancient Text (OT)


"'Neither,' he replied, 'but as commander of the army of the LORD I have now come.' Then Joshua fell facedown to the ground in reverence." - Joshua 5:14


The commander of the Lord's army. This is not a normal soldier. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. Joshua fell down and worshiped. The commander did not stop him. He told Joshua to take off his sandals. The ground was holy. This is the same figure from the burning bush. The same God. The same presence. The same Lord. He came with a sword. He came to lead. He came to fight. He came to win.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Then Jesus came to them and said, 'All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.'" - Matthew 28:18


The commander of the Lord's army has all authority. Jesus has all authority. The same figure. The same power. Before Jesus was born, He was standing on the road to Jericho with a sword. He is not just a helper. He is the commander. The battle is His. The victory is His. The authority is His.


The Verdict


The commander is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. He has all authority. He leads. He fights. He wins. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


What battle are you facing? What wall are you staring at? You might be asking, "God, are you on my side?" But the real question is different. Is He your commander? He is not a side. He is the leader. Let Him lead. The battle is already His.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the commander. I stop asking if you are on my side. I choose your side. I bow down. Lead me. Fight for me. The battle is yours. I trust you. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook


Three men refused to bow to a golden statue. The king was furious. He threw them into a furnace. It was so hot it killed the guards. The king looked in to watch them burn. But he saw four men. Walking. In the fire. The fourth looked like a god. This is one of the most dramatic encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Look! I see four men walking around in the fire, unbound and unharmed, and the fourth looks like a son of the gods." - Daniel 3:25


Four men. In the fire. The fourth was the pre-incarnate Christ. He was in the fire with them. He was walking with them. He was protecting them. They were not burned. They were not hurt. They came out without even the smell of smoke. The fire was real. The fourth man was real. The encounter was real. God showed up in the fire.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"And surely I am with you always, to the very end of the age." - Matthew 28:20


Jesus promised to be with us. Not to keep us out of the fire. To be in it. The fourth man in the fire is a picture of Jesus. He is the one who walks with us through the fire. He does not leave. He does not run. He stays. The fire is a shadow. The presence is the substance. The fourth man is Jesus.


The Verdict


The fourth man is a shadow. The presence of Jesus is the substance. He is with us in the fire. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you in a fire? Are you in a trial? Are you in a season that feels like it could consume you? You are not alone. There is a fourth man. He is walking with you. He is in the fire. He will not leave you. You will come out. And you will not even smell of smoke.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the fourth man. You are in the fire with me. Thank you. Thank you for walking with me. Thank you for staying. Thank you for not leaving. I am not alone. I am not afraid. You are here. Amen.

pages.body:
The Hook


Job lost everything. His children. His money. His health. He was in pain. He was angry. He asked God questions. And God answered. Not in a soft voice. In a whirlwind. The storm came. And God spoke. And Job got what he needed. He got God.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the LORD spoke to Job out of the storm." - Job 38:1


The LORD spoke. Out of the storm. Out of the whirlwind. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He spoke. He showed up. He came to Job. In the storm. In the pain. In the questions. He did not give easy answers. He gave Himself. Job saw God. Job heard God. Job encountered God. And it was enough.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"He got up, rebuked the wind and said to the waves, 'Quiet! Be still!' Then the wind died down and it was completely calm." - Mark 4:39


Jesus spoke to a storm. He calmed the wind. He calmed the waves. The same voice that spoke to Job spoke to the sea. The same God. The same power. The same presence. The storm is a shadow. The voice is the substance. The calm is the reality. The substance is Jesus.


The Verdict


The storm is a shadow. The voice is the substance. The calm is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you have questions for God? Do you feel like you cannot ask? Job asked. And God showed up. Not with easy answers. With Himself. He is not scared of your anger or your pain. He wants to speak to you. Listen. He is in the storm. He is in the whirlwind. He is speaking. Hear Him.


The Prayer


God, I have questions. I have pain. I have anger. I am done pretending. Speak to me. Show up. Not with easy answers. With yourself. I need you more than I need answers. Speak to me in the storm. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: The Voice in the Whirlwind

pages.body:
The Hook


Jacob was running away. He was scared. He was alone. He used a rock for a pillow. He fell asleep in the desert. And he dreamed. He saw a ladder. It reached from earth to heaven. Angels were going up and down on it. And God was at the top. This is one of the most famous encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"He had a dream in which he saw a stairway resting on the earth, with its top reaching to heaven, and the angels of God were ascending and descending on it." - Genesis 28:12


A ladder. A stairway. From earth to heaven. Angels going up and down. God at the top. This is a picture of connection. Heaven and earth were not far apart. They were connected. There was a way. There was a stairway. There was a path. The pre-incarnate Christ was at the top. He was the connection. He was the way.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"He then added, 'Very truly I tell you, you will see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.'" - John 1:51


Jesus said the ladder was Him. He is the stairway. He is the connection. He is the way between heaven and earth. He is the path between God and man. The ladder is a shadow. Jesus is the substance. The angels were going up and down on the ladder. They go up and down on the Son of Man. He is the connection. He is the way.


The Verdict


The ladder is a shadow. The Son of Man is the substance. He is the connection. He is the way. He is the stairway. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel disconnected from God? Do you feel like there is a gap? Do you feel like there is a distance? Remember the ladder. Remember Jesus. He is the connection. He is the way. He is the bridge. You can climb. You can come up. He made a way.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the ladder. You are the stairway. You are the connection. Thank you for making a way between heaven and earth. Thank you for making a way between me and God. I am climbing. I am coming up. I am with you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: The Ladder to Heaven

pages.body:
The Hook


Manoah and his wife could not have children. An angel appeared to the woman. He promised a son. She ran to tell her husband. He prayed. He wanted to see the angel for himself. The angel came back. And Manoah asked his name. The angel said something strange. "Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding."


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The angel of the LORD answered, 'Why do you ask my name? It is beyond understanding.'" - Judges 13:18


The angel's name was a secret. Beyond understanding. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He does not give His name. He is too big. Too holy. Too mysterious. Manoah offered a sacrifice. The angel ascended in the flame. And Manoah said, "We are doomed to die. We have seen God." Because he had. He had seen God face to face. The angel is God. The visible presence. The Visitor.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is himself God and is in closest relationship with the Father, has made him known." - John 1:18


Jesus makes God known. But before Jesus, the Son was already making God known. The Word was not silent before Bethlehem. He was speaking. He was showing up. He was visiting. The Son was in the Old Testament. He was the angel. He was the Visitor. He was the one with the secret name.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Son is the substance. The secret name is the substance. The visible presence is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you want to know God's name? Do you want to understand His mystery? You cannot fully. He is beyond understanding. But He has shown Himself. In Jesus. He is the visible presence. He is the one who makes God known. Look at Jesus. You will see the Father. You will know the name.


The Prayer


God, you are beyond understanding. Your name is a mystery. But you have shown yourself in Jesus. Thank you. Thank you for making yourself known. Thank you for the visible presence. I look at Jesus. I see you. I know you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: The Angel Who Would Not Give His Name

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The people were at the bottom of the mountain. The mountain was on fire. Smoke was rising. The ground was shaking. A voice was speaking. The people were terrified. They begged Moses to speak to God for them. They did not want to hear the voice themselves. This is one of the most powerful encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Mount Sinai was covered with smoke, because the LORD descended on it in fire. The smoke billowed up from it like smoke from a furnace, and the whole mountain trembled violently." - Exodus 19:18


God came down. On the mountain. In fire. In smoke. In thunder. The people shook. They stood at the bottom. They did not go up. Moses went up. God spoke. He gave the law. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He came down. He spoke. He showed up. The fire was real. The presence was real. The encounter was real.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"For you have not come to a mountain that can be touched and that is burning with fire... But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God." - Hebrews 12:18, 22


The mountain was terrifying. But we have not come to that mountain. We have come to a better one. The fire was real. But Jesus opened a different way. We do not stand at the bottom, scared. We come close. We come to God as a Father. The mountain is a shadow. The cross is the substance. The fear is the shadow. The grace is the substance.


The Verdict


The mountain is a shadow. The cross is the substance. The fear is the shadow. The grace is the substance. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel like God is a mountain you cannot climb? Like He is up there and you are down here and the smoke is too thick? The fire was real. But Jesus came to bring you up the mountain. You do not have to stand far away anymore. Come close. Come to the Father.


The Prayer


God, you are holy. I am not. Thank you that Jesus makes a way. Thank you that I do not have to stay at the bottom of the mountain, shaking. Bring me close. Let me come up. Let me see your face. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: The Fire on the Mountain

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The cloud came down. It covered the tent. The glory filled the tabernacle. Moses could not even go in. The presence of God was so heavy. So real. So thick. This is one of the most visual encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. Moses could not enter the tent of meeting because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle." - Exodus 40:34-35


The cloud came down. The glory filled the tent. Moses could not go in. The presence was too heavy. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He was in the cloud. He was in the glory. He was in the tent. He was with His people. Day after day. Leading them. Guiding them. Being with them. The cloud was the sign. The glory was the presence. The encounter was real.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The glory cloud came down on a tent. Jesus came down in flesh. The word "dwelling" here literally means "pitched his tent." Jesus is the new tent. He is the new cloud. He is the glory of God, walking. The cloud is a shadow. The flesh is the substance. The glory is the reality. The substance is Jesus.


The Verdict


The cloud is a shadow. The flesh is the substance. The glory is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you want to experience God's presence? Do you feel like you are outside the tent, looking in? The glory cloud was scary. But Jesus brought the glory down to us. He came near. He filled a human body. He can fill you. Come in. The tent is open.


The Prayer


God, fill me with your presence. I do not want to stand outside, looking in. I want to know your glory. Thank you that Jesus brought your glory down to me. Fill my tent. Fill me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: The Glory in the Cloud

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


Balaam was a prophet. He was on his way to curse God's people. He was riding a donkey. The donkey saw something Balaam could not. An angel. Standing in the road. With a drawn sword. The donkey stopped. Balaam beat it. And then the donkey spoke. And then Balaam saw. This is one of the strangest encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him... When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, it turned off the road into a field." - Numbers 22:22-23


The angel of the Lord stood in the road. With a sword. The donkey saw Him. The donkey turned. The donkey saved Balaam's life. Balaam was blind to the angel. He was blind to the danger. But the donkey saw. The angel was there. In person. With a sword. Ready to act. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He stands in the road. He opposes the wrong path. He protects. He warns. He saves.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"While they were going out, they met a man from Cyrene, named Simon, and they forced him to carry the cross." - Matthew 27:32


On the way to the cross, another man was pulled in. Simon of Cyrene carried the cross. He did not choose it. It was forced on him. The angel stood in the road. He opposed the wrong path. Jesus stood in the road of our sin. He took the sword. He took the curse. The angel in the road is a shadow. Jesus is the one who stands in our place.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. He stands in the road. He stands in our place. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


What road are you on? Is there an angel standing in it? Is God trying to stop you? Sometimes the thing that stops you is the thing that saves you. The donkey was smarter than the prophet. Listen. God may be standing in your road. He is not trying to ruin your journey. He is trying to save it.


The Prayer


God, thank you for standing in my road. Thank you for the warnings. Thank you for the things that stop me. Help me to see. Help me to listen. You are not trying to ruin my journey. You are trying to save it. I will listen. I will turn. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: The Angel in the Road

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


Elijah was scared. He had just won a huge victory. Fire from heaven. The people worshiped. Then a queen threatened him. He ran. He hid in a cave. He was depressed. He wanted to die. And God came to him. Not in the wind. Not in the earthquake. Not in the fire. In a gentle whisper. This is one of the most intimate encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"After the earthquake came a fire, but the LORD was not in the fire. And after the fire came a gentle whisper." - 1 Kings 19:12


A gentle whisper. A still, small voice. God was in the whisper. Not in the noise. Not in the drama. Not in the big things. In the quiet. In the small. In the gentle. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He comes in the whisper. He speaks in the quiet. He meets us in the stillness. The whisper is the encounter. The quiet is the presence.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


God showed up in a whisper. Then He showed up in a baby. Not in a palace. In a stable. Not in the loud. In the quiet. The gentle whisper of Elijah is a shadow. The flesh of Jesus is the substance. God is not always in the loud things. He is in the small things. He is in the quiet. He is in the person.


The Verdict


The whisper is a shadow. The person is the substance. God comes in the quiet. God comes in the small. God comes in the stillness. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you looking for God in the big things? In the loud things? In the dramatic things? He is in the quiet. He is in the whisper. He is in the small. He is in the person. Listen. He is speaking. Not in the earthquake. In the stillness. Be still. Hear Him.


The Prayer


God, help me to hear the whisper. I am looking for the big things. I am waiting for the loud things. But you are in the quiet. You are in the small. Speak to me in the silence. I am listening. I am still. I am here. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: The Voice in the Whisper

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


Solomon built the temple. It was beautiful. It was huge. It was the house of God. And when it was finished, Solomon prayed. He asked God to fill it. And fire came down. From heaven. And the glory filled the temple. This is one of the most powerful encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices, and the glory of the LORD filled the temple." - 2 Chronicles 7:1


Fire came down. The glory filled the temple. God showed up. He filled the house. The house was His. The glory was His. The fire was His. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He came down. He filled the temple. He showed up. The fire was real. The glory was real. The encounter was real.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Don't you know that you yourselves are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in your midst?" - 1 Corinthians 3:16


We are the temple. God lives in us. The fire is in us. The glory is in us. The temple is a shadow. The Spirit in us is the substance. The fire that filled the temple fills us. The glory that filled the temple fills us. The presence that filled the temple fills us. We are the temple. We are the house. We are the fire.


The Verdict


The temple is a shadow. The Spirit in us is the substance. We are the temple




….




CONTINUED — DAY 15 (FINISHED)


The Verdict (continued)


We are the temple. The fire fills us. The glory fills us. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you know that you are the temple? Do you know that the fire fills you? Do you know that the glory fills you? You are the house of God. The fire came down. The glory filled the temple. The Spirit fills you. You are the temple. You are the fire. You are the glory. Live like it. Carry His presence into every room you walk into.


The Prayer


God, thank you that I am the temple. Thank you that the fire fills me. Thank you that the glory fills me. Fill me with your presence. Fill me with your Spirit. I am your house. I am your fire. I am your glory. Let your presence spill out of me everywhere I go. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: The Glory in the Temple

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


A king was having a party. He was drinking. He was mocking God. He was using the sacred cups from the temple. And then he saw it. A hand. Writing on the wall. A finger. Writing letters. In the air. The king was terrified. His knees knocked. His face went pale. This is one of the strangest and scariest encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Suddenly the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall, near the lampstand in the royal palace. The king watched the hand as it wrote. His face turned pale and he was so frightened that his legs became weak and his knees were knocking." - Daniel 5:5-6


A hand appeared. A finger wrote. On the wall. In the palace. In front of the king. The message was judgment. The king was weighed and found wanting. The hand was God's. The finger was God's. The writing was God's. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He showed up. In a hand. In a finger. In letters. He wrote. He spoke. He judged.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"But Jesus bent down and started to write on the ground with his finger." - John 8:6


A hand wrote on a wall. A finger wrote on the ground. When the woman caught in adultery was brought to Jesus, He wrote on the ground with His finger. The same finger. The same God. He wrote judgment once. He wrote grace once. The finger is the same. The God is the same. The hand on the wall is a shadow. The finger on the ground is the substance. Jesus is the finger of God.


The Verdict


The hand is a shadow. The finger is the substance. God writes. God speaks. God shows up. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Is God writing on your wall? Is He trying to get your attention? Is He speaking? Do not ignore it. The hand was a warning. It was a message. God is speaking to you. Listen. He is writing. He is showing up. Do not be like the king. Do not be found wanting. Respond.


The Prayer


God, I see your hand. I hear your voice. I do not want to be found wanting. I do not want to ignore you. Write on my heart. Write your truth. Write your grace. I am listening. I am responding. I am yours. Amen.
pages.title: Day 16: The Hand That Wrote

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at the fire on Day 07. But there is more. The king did not just see four men. He saw the fourth man. And the fourth man was not a normal man. He was the Visitor. He was the pre-incarnate Christ. He was in the fire. With His people. And the fire did not touch them.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"He said, 'Look, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they are not hurt, and the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'" - Daniel 3:25


The fourth man. Walking. In the fire. Not burned. Not hurt. The king was amazed. He did not know who it was. But he knew it was not normal. It was a god. It was the son of the gods. It was the Visitor. The one who shows up. The one who stays. The one who walks through fire. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He was in the fire. He was with His people. He was protecting them. He was present.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"I am with you always, to the very end of the age." - Matthew 28:20


Jesus said this to His disciples. He did not say, "I will keep you out of trouble." He said, "I am with you always." The fourth man in the fire is a promise. I will be with you. In the fire. In the trouble. In the pain. I will not leave. This is the heart of God. This is the Visitor. This is Jesus.


The Verdict


The fourth man is a shadow. The presence of Jesus is the substance. He is with us in the fire. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you in a fire? Are you in the flames? You are not alone. There is a fourth man. He is walking with you. He is not going to pull you out every time. But He will be with you in it. He will not leave you. You are safe. Not because the fire is gone. Because He is there.


The Prayer


Jesus, thank you for being the fourth man. Thank you for walking with me in the fire. Thank you that I am not alone. I will not be burned. I will come out. You are with me. I am safe. Amen.
pages.title: Day 17: The Man in the Fiery Furnace

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at Job on Day 08. But there is more. Job did not just hear a voice. Job saw God. He said, "My ears had heard of you, but now my eyes have seen you." That is the encounter. That is the point. Job did not get answers. He got God. He saw the pre-incarnate Christ. In the whirlwind. In the storm. And it changed him.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"My ears had heard of you but now my eyes have seen you. Therefore I despise myself and repent in dust and ashes." - Job 42:5-6


Job saw God. He did not just hear about Him. He saw Him. The encounter was real. The sight was real. The presence was real. Job was changed. He repented. He was humbled. He was satisfied. He had seen God. The pre-incarnate Christ showed up in the whirlwind. He showed Himself to Job. And Job saw Him.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father." - John 14:9


Jesus said if you have seen Him, you have seen the Father. Job saw the Son. He saw the pre-incarnate Christ. He saw the visible presence of God. He saw the one who would later say, "Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father." The whirlwind is a shadow. The face of Jesus is the substance. The sight is the reality. The substance is Jesus.


The Verdict


The whirlwind is a shadow. The face of Jesus is the substance. The sight is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you want to see God? Do you want more than hearing about Him? Look at Jesus. He is the visible presence. He is the one who shows up. He is the one who reveals the Father. If you want to see God, look at the Son. He is the sight. He is the encounter. He is the one your eyes can see.


The Prayer


Jesus, I want to see you. I want more than hearing about you. I want to see you. Show yourself to me. Reveal the Father to me. I look at you. I see God. I see the Father. I see the visible presence. Thank you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: The Voice in the Storm

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


Peter was in prison. Chained between two soldiers. In the dark. He was going to die. The church was praying. An angel appeared. The chains fell off. The doors opened. Peter walked out. He did not know if it was real. He thought he was dreaming. But it was real. The angel was real. The Visitor was there.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'See, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.'" - Exodus 23:20


God sent an angel to guard His people. To lead them. To protect them. This is the same pattern. God sends His angel. The angel goes before them. The angel opens doors. The angel breaks chains. God is not far. He is active. He is working. He is showing up. The pre-incarnate Christ is the angel. He is the one who goes before. He is the one who opens. He is the one who frees.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He struck Peter on the side and woke him up. 'Quick, get up!' he said, and the chains fell off Peter's wrists." - Acts 12:7


An angel appeared to Peter. Chains fell off. The gates opened. Peter was free. The same pattern. The angel of the Lord. The Visitor. He came to set the prisoner free. He came to open the door. He came to break the chain. This is God. He shows up for the prisoner. He shows up for the hopeless. He shows up.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. He opens doors. He breaks chains. He frees. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you in a prison? A prison of fear? Of addiction? Of guilt? Of shame? You are not alone. There is an angel. There is a Visitor. He is coming to open the door. He is coming to break the chain. He is coming to set you free. Get up. The chains are falling. Walk out.


The Prayer


Jesus, I am in a prison. I need freedom. I need the chains to fall off. I need the doors to open. Come to me. Set me free. Break the chains. Open the door. Let me walk out. I am getting up. I am walking out. I am free. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: The Angel Who Opened the Prison

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The people were in the desert. They were thirsty. They complained. And God gave them water from a rock. But that rock did not stay put. It followed them. It traveled with them. It was there every time they needed it. This is strange. And it is a picture of the pre-incarnate Christ.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Behold, I will stand before you there on the rock at Horeb, and you shall strike the rock, and water shall come out of it, and the people will drink." - Exodus 17:6


The rock was there. It was struck. It gave water. But the rock did not stay. It followed them. It was with them. It provided for them. It gave them water. This is a picture. It is a picture of a God who is always there. A God who travels with His people. A God who is with them in the desert. The rock is the pre-incarnate Christ. He was with them. He followed them. He provided for them.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"And they all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ." - 1 Corinthians 10:4


Paul says the rock was Christ. He is the rock. He is the one who follows us. He is the one who is with us. He is the one who gives water. The rock followed them. Jesus follows us. The rock gave water. Jesus gives living water. The rock is a shadow. Jesus is the substance. He is the rock. He follows us. He is with us.


The Verdict


The rock is a shadow. The following is the substance. Jesus follows us. Jesus is with us. Jesus gives water. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you know that Jesus follows you? Do you know that He is with you? Do you know that He gives water? He is the rock. He is following you. He is with you. He is providing. You are not alone in the desert. The rock is there. Drink. Be satisfied. He has not left you.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the rock. You follow me. You are with me. You give water. Thank you. Thank you for following me. Thank you for being with me. Thank you for the water. I am drinking. I am satisfied. You are with me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: The Rock That Followed

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The temple was the house of God. His presence filled it. The cloud. The fire. The glory. But there came a moment when the glory left. The temple was still there. The building was still standing. But God was gone. The house was empty. This is one of the saddest encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The glory of the LORD went up from within the city and stopped above the mountain east of it." - Ezekiel 11:23


The glory of the Lord left. The presence of God lifted. He was not there anymore. The temple was empty. This is a sad moment. But it is an important moment. It shows that God is not tied to a building. He is not in a box. He is a person. He is the Visitor. He can leave. He can return. And He can come in a new way. The glory left. But the glory would return.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Look! Your house is left to you desolate. For I tell you, you will not see me again until you say, 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.'" - Matthew 23:38-39


Jesus spoke to the temple. He said it was empty. The glory had left. But He also said He would come back. He is the glory. He is the one who fills the house. He is the Visitor. He can leave. He can return. He will return. He is not done with us. He is not done with the temple. He is not done with His people. The glory left. But the glory is coming back.


The Verdict


The glory leaving is a shadow. The glory returning is the substance. He leaves. He returns. He fills. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Have you felt like the glory has left? Like God is far away? Like the house is empty? He is not gone. He is coming back. He is the Visitor. He is not limited to a building. He is not limited to a place. He is a person. He is Jesus. He will return. He will fill the house again. Wait for Him.


The Prayer


God, I feel like the glory has left. I feel like the house is empty. But you are the Visitor. You are the glory. You are the presence. Come back. Fill me again. Fill your house. Fill your people. I am waiting. I am ready. Come. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: The Glory That Left

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


Daniel saw a vision. He was in exile. He was in a foreign land. And he saw a throne. And he saw someone on the throne. Someone like a son of man. Coming with the clouds of heaven. And He was given authority. Glory. And a kingdom that would never end. This is one of the most important encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"In my vision at night I looked, and there before me was one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was led into his presence. He was given authority, glory and sovereign power; all nations and peoples of every language worshiped him." - Daniel 7:13-14


The Son of Man. Coming with the clouds. Given authority. Given glory. Given a kingdom. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. Daniel saw Him. On the throne. In the glory. With the authority. This is the one who would come. This is the one who would rule. This is the one who would save. Daniel saw Jesus. Before He was born. On the throne.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Then the high priest said to him, 'I charge you under oath by the living God: Tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God.' 'You have said so,' Jesus replied. 'But I say to all of you: From now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Mighty One and coming on the clouds of heaven.'" - Matthew 26:63-64


Jesus said it was Him. He is the Son of Man. He is the one on the throne. He is the one coming with the clouds. Daniel saw Him. Daniel saw Jesus. The vision is a shadow. The throne is the substance. The Son of Man is the reality. The substance is Jesus.


The Verdict


The vision is a shadow. The throne is the substance. The Son of Man is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you need to see the throne? Do you need to see who is in charge? Look at Daniel's vision. Look at Jesus. He is on the throne. He has the authority. He has the glory. He has the kingdom. Nothing is out of His control. Nothing is outside His rule. He is the Son of Man. He is the King. Trust Him.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the Son of Man. You are on the throne. You have the authority. You have the glory. You have the kingdom. I look at you. I see the King. I trust you. Nothing is out of your control. You are on the throne. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: The Son of Man on the Throne

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


A garden. A man. A woman. A tree. A choice. And a God who walked in the cool of the day. This is the first encounter. The first Visitor. Before the tent. Before the fire. Before the ladder. There was a garden. And God was there. Walking. In person.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the man and his wife heard the sound of the LORD God as he was walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and they hid from the LORD God among the trees of the garden." - Genesis 3:8


God was walking. In the garden. With people. This is the first relationship. God with Adam and Eve. He was not far. He was near. He was present. He was in the garden. And He was walking. This is the heart of everything. God wants to be with us. He wants to walk with us. He wants to be near. The pre-incarnate Christ was walking in the garden. He was the one they heard. He was the one they hid from. He is the one who came to find them.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, 'Look! God's dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God.'" - Revelation 21:3


The garden is the beginning. The New Jerusalem is the end. God with His people. Walking with them. The garden was the first shadow. The city is the final picture. God wants to be with us. He has always wanted it. He will always want it. The Visitor in the garden is the same Visitor in the city. He is the one who walks with us. He is Jesus.


The Verdict


The garden is a shadow. The city is the substance. The walking God is the pattern. The substance is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel far from God? Do you feel like you are hiding in the trees? He is walking. He is looking for you. He is not angry. He is looking. Come out. He wants to walk with you. He wants to be with you. That is the whole story. Come out of hiding. Walk with Him.


The Prayer


God, I have been hiding. I have been in the trees. I have been afraid. But you are walking. You are looking. You are calling. I am coming out. Walk with me. Be with me. I want to be near you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: The Man in the Garden

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at Hagar on Day 04. But there is more. Hagar was not just seen. She was saved. She was in the desert. She was dying of thirst. She put her son under a bush. She sat down and cried. She could not watch him die. And God heard. And the angel called. And a well opened. This is one of the most tender encounters in the Bible.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. So she went and filled the skin with water and gave the boy a drink." - Genesis 21:19


Hagar was dying. Her son was dying. She cried. She gave up. And God opened her eyes. And she saw a well. The water was there all along. She just could not see it. God showed up. God provided. God saved. The pre-incarnate Christ was there. He was the one who heard. He was the one who opened her eyes. He was the one who gave the water.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"Whoever drinks the water I give them will never thirst. Indeed, the water I give them will become in them a spring of water welling up to eternal life." - John 4:14


Jesus is the water. He is the well. He is the spring. Hagar saw a well. We see Jesus. The well is a shadow. The water is the substance. The spring is the reality. The substance is Jesus. He opens our eyes. He gives us water. He saves us.


The Verdict


The well is a shadow. The water is the substance. The spring is the reality. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Are you crying? Are you giving up? Are you in the desert? Do you feel like you cannot see a way out? God is opening your eyes. There is a well. There is water. There is a spring. It is right there. You just cannot see it yet. He is with you. He hears you. He will open your eyes. You will see the well.


The Prayer


God, I am crying. I am giving up. I am in the desert. Open my eyes. Let me see the well. Let me see the water. Let me see the spring. You are here. You hear me. You will save me. I am looking. I am seeing. I am drinking. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: The Angel in the Desert

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at Balaam on Day 13. But there is more. The angel was not just in the road. The angel was standing against Balaam. He was blocking the wrong path. He was protecting the people of God. The angel was not a passive observer. The angel was an active warrior. This is a picture of the pre-incarnate Christ.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him... When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, it turned off the road into a field." - Numbers 22:22-23


The angel stood in the road. With a sword. He opposed Balaam. He blocked the path. He protected God's people. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He stands in the road. He opposes the wrong. He protects the right. He fights. He defends. He stands. The sword is in His hand. The battle is His. The victory is His.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"In his right hand he held seven stars, and coming out of his mouth was a sharp, double-edged sword. His face was like the sun shining in all its brilliance." - Revelation 1:16


Jesus has a sword. It comes out of His mouth. It is the word of God. He stands in the road. He opposes the wrong. He protects the right. The angel with a sword is a shadow. Jesus with a sword is the substance. He fights for us. He defends us. He stands in the road.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. He stands. He fights. He defends. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you know that Jesus fights for you? Do you know that He stands in the road? Do you know that He opposes the wrong? You are not alone in the battle. He is with you. He is fighting. He is defending. He is standing. Trust Him. The battle is His.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the one with the sword. You stand in the road. You fight for me. You defend me. Thank you. Thank you for fighting. Thank you for defending. Thank you for standing. I am not alone. The battle is yours. I trust you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: The Sword in the Road

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at the burning bush on Day 03. But there is more. The fire did not consume the bush. The fire was real. The bush stayed green. The presence of God was in the bush, and the bush was not destroyed. This is a picture of the pre-incarnate Christ. The presence of God in the person. The fire in the bush. The God in the man.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Moses saw that though the bush was on fire it did not burn up." - Exodus 3:2


The bush was on fire. The bush did not burn up. The fire was real. The bush was not. The presence was real. The bush was not consumed. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He is the fire. He is the presence. He is in the bush. And the bush is not destroyed. He fills. He does not destroy. He makes holy. He does not consume.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The Word became flesh. The fire became a body. The presence became a person. The bush was not consumed. The body was not destroyed. The fire was in the bush. The God was in the man. The bush is a shadow. The body is the substance. The fire is the presence. The person is Jesus.


The Verdict


The bush is a shadow. The body is the substance. The fire is the presence. The person is Jesus. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you feel like the fire of God would consume you? Do you feel like His presence would destroy you? Look at the bush. It stayed green. His presence does not destroy you. It fills you. It makes you holy. It makes you alive. You will not be consumed. You will be changed. Let the fire come.


The Prayer


God, thank you that your fire does not consume me. Thank you that your presence fills me. Thank you that you make me holy. I am not afraid of the fire. I welcome it. Fill me. Change me. Make me like you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: The Fire That Did Not Consume

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


There is a moment in the Old Testament that stops you cold. A man is speaking. He says something huge. And it changes everything about how we read the Bible. He says God appeared to Abraham. But he says it was a man. He says it was two men. And one was God. This is the ultimate encounter. The pre-incarnate Christ in person.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The LORD appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre while he was sitting at the entrance to his tent in the heat of the day." - Genesis 18:1


The LORD appeared. As what? We read the next verse. Abraham looked up and saw three men. One of them is the LORD. The text is clear. God appeared as a man. God walked. God talked. God ate. This is not a vision or a dream. This is physical. Tangible. Real. The pre-incarnate Christ was in the tent. He was in the body. He was the man. He was God.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"No one has ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who is himself God and is in closest relationship with the Father, has made him known." - John 1:18


Jesus is the one who makes God known. But before Jesus, the Son was already making God known. The Word was not silent before Bethlehem. He was speaking. He was showing up. He was visiting. The Son was in the Old Testament. He was the Visitor. He was the man in the tent. He was God.


The Verdict


The man in the tent is a shadow. The Son in the flesh is the substance. God appears. God walks. God talks. God eats. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Does the Old Testament feel like a different God? Like a different book? Look closer. He is the same. The Visitor in the tent is the Man on the road. He has always wanted to be seen. Open your eyes. See Him. He is on every page. He is in every encounter. He is the one who shows up.


The Prayer


Jesus, thank you that you were not silent before Bethlehem. Thank you that you showed up. Thank you that you were always making God known. Open my eyes to see you on every page. You are the Visitor. You are the one in the tent. You are the one in the flesh. I see you. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: The Man Who Was God

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


We looked at Peter on Day 19. But there is more. The angel did not just open the door. The angel led him out. Step by step. Through the gates. Into the street. And then the angel left. Peter was free. The encounter was complete. This is a picture of the pre-incarnate Christ. He does not just open the door. He leads you out.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"Then the LORD said to Moses, 'See, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.'" - Exodus 23:20


The angel goes ahead. The angel guards. The angel brings. The angel leads. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He goes before us. He guards us. He brings us. He leads us. He does not just open the door. He walks us through. He does not just break the chain. He leads us out. He is the guide. He is the leader. He is the one who goes before.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"When Jesus spoke again to the people, he said, 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness, but will have the light of life.'" - John 8:12


Jesus is the light. He leads. He guides. He goes before. The angel led Peter out. Jesus leads us out. The angel went ahead. Jesus goes ahead. The angel brought him to the place. Jesus brings us to the place. The angel is a shadow. Jesus is the substance. He leads. He guides. He goes before.


The Verdict


The angel is a shadow. The Christ is the substance. He goes before. He leads. He guides. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you need a guide? Do you need someone to go before you? Do you need to be led out? Jesus goes before you. He leads you. He guides you. He does not just open the door. He walks you through. Follow Him. He knows the way. He is the way. He will lead you out.


The Prayer


Jesus, you go before me. You lead me. You guide me. Thank you. Thank you for going before. Thank you for leading. Thank you for guiding. I follow you. I trust you. Lead me out. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: The Angel in the Prison

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The glory left the temple. We looked at that on Day 21. But there is more. The glory did not stay gone. The prophets promised it would return. God would come back. He would fill the house again. He would dwell with His people again. This is the hope. The glory returns. This is the pre-incarnate Christ. He leaves. He returns. He fills.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"The glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east." - Ezekiel 43:4


The glory returned. The presence came back. The house was filled again. This is a picture. It is a picture of hope. It is a picture of return. It is a picture of Jesus. He leaves. He returns. He fills. The glory left. The glory returned. The pattern is the same. The presence is the same. The God is the same.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"On the last and greatest day of the festival, Jesus stood and said in a loud voice, 'Let anyone who is thirsty come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from within them.'" - John 7:37-38


Jesus is the glory. He is the presence. He is the one who fills. The glory returned to the temple. Jesus came to the temple. The glory filled the house. Jesus filled the house. The glory is a shadow. Jesus is the substance. He returns. He fills. He is the glory. He is the presence.


The Verdict


The returning glory is a shadow. The returning Christ is the substance. He returns. He fills. He is the presence. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


Do you need the glory to return? Do you need the presence to come back? Do you need the house to be filled? He returns. He always returns. He is the glory. He is the presence. He will fill you. He will fill your house. He will fill your life. Wait for Him. He is coming. He is returning.


The Prayer


God, return. Return to my house. Return to my heart. Fill me with your glory. Fill me with your presence. You left. But you promised to return. I am waiting. I am ready. Come back. Fill me. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: The Glory That Returned

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Hook


The ultimate encounter is not a bush. It is not a ladder. It is not a fire. It is not a whirlwind. The ultimate encounter is God in a body. The Word in flesh. The invisible in a person. The eternal in a baby. This is the encounter that all the others were pointing to. This is Jesus.


The Ancient Text (OT)


"For to us a child is born, to us a son is given, and the government will be on his shoulders. And he will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace." - Isaiah 9:6


A child. A son. Mighty God. Everlasting Father. Prince of Peace. This is the ultimate encounter. The child is God. The son is eternal. The baby is the Creator. This is the encounter that all the other encounters were pointing to. The bush. The ladder. The tent. The fire. The whirlwind. The hand. The rock. The angel. All of them. All pointing to this. The child. The son. The Savior.


The Fulfillment (NT)


"The Word became flesh and made his dwelling among us. We have seen his glory, the glory of the one and only Son, who came from the Father, full of grace and truth." - John 1:14


The Word became flesh. The encounter became a person. The shadow became substance. The picture became reality. The bush became a body. The ladder became a life. The tent became a person. The fire became a friend. The whirlwind became a whisper. The hand became a healer. The rock became a Savior. The angel became a brother. The ultimate encounter is Jesus. And He is here. He is with us. He is not far. He is near. He is the one your heart is looking for.


The Verdict


All the encounters are shadows. Jesus is the substance. All the encounters point to Him. All the encounters are fulfilled in Him. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The substance is Jesus.


The Resonance


You have been looking for an encounter. You have been searching for God. He is not








CONTINUED — DAY 30 (FINISHED)


The Resonance (continued)


You have been looking for an encounter. You have been searching for God. He is not far. He is not hiding. He has been showing up all along. In the garden. In the tent. In the fire. In the whisper. In the child. He is the one your heart is looking for. Stop searching in the wrong places. Stop looking for Him in the stars, in the universe, in the vague force. Look at Jesus. He is the ultimate encounter. He is the one who shows up. Open your eyes. Open your heart. He is here.


The Prayer


Jesus, you are the ultimate encounter. You are the one I have been looking for. You are the one my heart has been searching for. I found you. Or rather, you found me. Thank you. Thank you for showing up. Thank you for the garden. Thank you for the tent. Thank you for the fire. Thank you for the whisper. Thank you for the child. Thank you for being the Word made flesh. Thank you for being the visible God. Thank you for being Jesus. I receive you. I believe in you. I follow you. Amen.



END MATTER




The 30-Day Encounter Challenge


You have journeyed through 30 divine encounters. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It is the perfect follow-up. It shows you the ultimate encounter. It shows you the Word made flesh. It shows you Jesus, the visible God. As you read, look for the encounters. Look for the moments where people meet Jesus. Look for the ones who see Him. Look for the ones who believe. And then ask yourself, "Have I encountered Him?" He is not far. He is in the book. He is in the room. He is here.


A Note on Faith


The encounters are evidence. They are evidence of a God who shows up. They are evidence of a God who is not distant. They are evidence of a God who wants to be known. But evidence does not save you. The encounters point to a person. The encounters point to Jesus. You can study the encounters and still miss the Encounter. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The encounters are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice. He is knocking. Will you open?


About the Author


Christine A. writes for the spiritually curious. He is passionate about showing people the hidden wisdom of the Bible. He lives with his family and enjoys good coffee and long conversations with skeptics. He believes that honest questions deserve honest answers.


Coming Next: The New Believer Edition


If you have made a decision to follow Jesus, the next step is to build a strong foundation. The New Believer Edition takes the same 30 encounters and shows you how to apply them to your new life. It is a 30 day guide to understanding what Jesus did for you. It will help you grow in your faith and trust in God.
